note: The bar this kit is measured against, as a record and not as pixels. Mobbin licences a screenshot to its subscriber, and this is public source, so no image byte is committed here: each entry names the bytes in the reference store, and `npm run check:references` proves the store still holds exactly those bytes. The `why` column is why the screen was chosen for this family; `ours` is what the kit draws today against it, which is the gap the review looks at.

entries.why: Phone rows carrying key, priority chevron, status pill and date in a small footprint under a saved-view selector.
entries.ours: Row carries an eyebrow, a title, up to two cell lines and one trailing element; nothing reserves a right-aligned date column or a status pill beside it, and Section has no group header with a count.

entries.why: Watchlist card with total change, rows of ticker, name, sparkline and coloured change pill, plus Add symbol and Edit list: the phone watchlist.
entries.ours: StatTile, Sparkline and Badge draw those three pieces, and Sparkline's picture is decoration rather than a DOM attribute since 4abccdd; the row that holds ticker, name and sparkline in one measure is the composition the app writes, and the gallery shows them one specimen apart.

entries.why: One large card for the book in progress, its progress bar and a single "Playing · 18 min left" button; the mini player persists while browsing.
entries.ours: MiniPlayer holds cover, title, elapsed and remaining and one control, collapsed over a list and expanded with its scrubber; its controls are now named in the person's language and reachable one by one (fe19dc4), and its artwork is the caller's, so a photographed strip is only as real as the picture the app supplies.

entries.why: The pack's own artwork is the hero, with price, sold count and one full-width buy verb under it: the cover card a phone shop leads with.
entries.ours: MediaHero draws a picture, its caption and one control beneath the picture, and ProductCard draws cover, name, price and option chips inside a bordered card. Nothing in the kit writes a price chip or a title over the artwork, and a card that cannot be bought says so in a line under the picture rather than on the tile itself.

entries.why: A dense watchlist table: right-aligned tabular numerals, a coloured change beside every amount, a sparkline column and named column headers.
entries.ours: DataList is a grouped row list with saved views, ordering, selection and per-row actions; a row is a title, up to a few cells and a trailing element. It has no column header row and no right-aligned numeric column, so two rows' figures share no baseline.

entries.why: A sheet that lives over the map it came from, draggable, carrying a plate chip, a status headline and its own actions.
entries.ours: DetailSheet is DetailSurface in modal mode: the same header, body and foot verb, opened and closed. It has no detent, no drag, and nothing behind it changes while it moves — the sheet arrives rather than being pulled up.

entries.why: A drawer that holds a record with a state — since, revenue, a membership card reading Used 1/4 and Renews on — over the schedule it opened from.
entries.ours: SidePanel is that same surface docked at a width: a column of whatever the caller passes, closed by the same verb. It owns no labelled summary block and no meter of its own; the record-with-a-state layout is still written by the app.

entries.why: The nearest modal surface the pool holds: a sheet that dims what is behind it, owns the decision, and changes the surface beneath while it is open. The pool shows no decision dialog at all — no screen in refs/apps/*/refs.json names a dialog, modal, alert or confirmation — so the dialog's own bar is the platform's alert idiom plus this craft board, and the device leg has to confirm it.
entries.ours: ConfirmDialog holds a title, a body, the reason the write refuses or takes away, a confirm verb, a cancel, a destructive tone and a busy state that refuses the second activation; a busy backdrop routes cancel instead of dismissing. The reference is a sheet, not a decision dialog, and this row says so.

entries.why: One screen that leads with the thing in progress and ends in a three-item bottom bar — the phone home this kit's Screen, Home and TabBar have to compose.
entries.ours: TabBar draws two to five destinations, icon above label, inside the device's bottom inset, `raised` when it floats over the content, with the tab's badge text where it has one. What the screen still shows and the kit does not is the bar sitting under a persistent mini player: the kit draws the two a page apart.

entries.why: A phone directory of destinations: search, one featured card, category chips, then icon rows each carrying a subtitle and a chevron.
entries.ours: Row draws a title, up to a few cell lines and a chevron; MoreFilters gathers choice groups behind one verb. The kit has no icon-row preset that carries a subtitle beside the glyph and no counted rail — the destinations a phone navigates by are still composed per app.

entries.why: A search that states the count it filtered, a status badge only where it means something, and a clear path to each row's details.
entries.ours: SearchField prints the query, the count the query narrowed to inside the strip, a busy mark while a request is in flight, and a clear that empties the query and asks for the whole set again. It has no cancel that hands the keyboard back, and the strip owns no filter pills beside it.

entries.why: Filter pills that print the value they are filtering by, a Reset filters link beside them, and one filled action on the same line.
entries.ours: ChoiceChips shows which chip is selected and refuses a disabled one with its reason; MoreFilters holds groups behind one verb. A selected chip still prints no value, and nothing beside the row offers a reset — a filter you can only read is a second implementation of the screen's state.

entries.why: The hierarchy a field sits in: available balance above the control, the amount and fee lines under it, one full-width confirm. The pool shows no inline field error anywhere, so this pixel is the field's hierarchy and the refusal grammar comes from Klook's sold-out days — unavailability shown in the row it belongs to, with its reason, never as a toast.
entries.ours: FormField puts one label, one control, its help and its refusal in one measure, and the refusal names the rule; ServerField shows what the server refused in the same shape. There is no inline-affordance slot for a balance or a limit and no foot total beside the confirm verb.

entries.why: A vertical step rail with the current step expanded and a plain sentence under it saying what happens next.
entries.ours: Stepper marks first, middle and last, names the step it refuses, keeps its own revision, and offers Save & exit for a write with an unknown outcome. It does not say what happens next under the step the person is on.

entries.why: The empty state as the headline of the screen with exactly one primary action, not a caption under an empty frame.
entries.ours: EmptyState takes a title, a body, one action and a secondary, and the state views keep the screen's header alive above it. It has no illustration slot and no spot art; a screen that is empty because a filter refused is a different model line, not a different drawing.

entries.why: The only notice any screen in the pool carries: a band with its own type over the content it belongs to. No screen in refs/apps/*/refs.json shows a toast, snack or banner, so this row's pixel is a notice in place, not a timed one.
entries.ours: Notice is an in-flow band with a tone, an optional title, its own action and an announcement politeness; it never removes layout without saying so. It has no timed presence and no elevation above the surface — a Notice stays where the screen put it.

entries.why: A streak strip over stat tiles and per-track horizontal bars, each with its number printed beside it.
entries.ours: ProgressMeter draws the fraction it was given, the number it came with, a tone for what kind of measure it is, and a marked rail for a stepper's progress; it refuses a fraction it cannot vouch for rather than inventing one. It is one meter per call: the strip over three bars is the composition no page of the kit shows yet.
